newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Colruyt says first-half profit up 11.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Colruyt says first-half profit up 11.6 percent.

text.p: Belgium's third largest retailer Colruyt said on Wednesday its first half 1996-1997 consolidated net profit rose 11.6 percent to 1.105 billion Belgian francs ($34.3 million) from 990 million in the same year-ago period.
The rise was broadly in line with analysts' expectations.
Colruyt said in a statement it expected full year consolidated net profit to be at least 2.15 billion francs compared to 1.934 the previous year.

First half turnover rose to 33 billion francs from 28.5 billion, though on a comparable basis -- by excluding distribution group Ripotot France which the Belgian retailer bought last year - it was 31.1 billion francs.
Results and turnover from its Dolmen Computer Applications, Druco and Droomland subsidiaries were developing favourably and were in line with forecasts, Colruyt said.

For the first nine months of the 1996/1997 financial year, which ends on March 31, turnover at Colruyt sales outlets increased eight percent, which the statement said was in line with forecasts. Annual results are published at the end of June.
Shares in the retailer rose 50 Belgian francs to 14,000 on the Brussels bourse on Wednesday. ($1=32.19 Belgian Franc)
